name: Fjällräven
why: Swedish outdoor house from 1960: the G-1000 waxed poly-cotton, the Greenland jacket and the Kånken, with 21 US stores of its own.
origin: Founded in 1960 in Örnsköldsvik, Sweden by Åke Nordin.

onething.p: Greenland Jacket (G-1000, 1968); the Kånken backpack (1978) is the house's best-known product overall but is not clothing

notes.craft: Thread proposed 2 (2026-10-10): Fjällräven names no factories, makers or mills on its product pages and states no country of origin on any of the 246 men's styles read; its production page speaks only of a Code of Conduct, audits and FLA membership. What it does document is a dated, placed founding (1960, Åke Nordin, Örnsköldsvik) and its own fabric system (G-1000 with Greenland Wax), which is tech rather than craft. cities: 21 stores across the US, including Boston, New York, Ann Arbor · department stores, independent shops, and its own site

marks: G-1000 family (Original, Lite, HeavyDuty, Silent, Stretch, Lite Stretch, Air Stretch) with Greenland Wax re-proofing

craft_evidence.owned: no (nothing on the brand site or in the Fenix Outdoor 2024 annual report says Fjällräven owns apparel making; the report mentions a group partnership with Viomoda, Plovdiv, Bulgaria as a first step to European apparel production, not attributed to a Fjällräven range)
craft_evidence.makers: no (no maker or factory named on the 246 PDPs; sustainable-production page names none, only Code of Conduct, audits, FLA membership since 2013)
craft_evidence.mills: no (mills not named; trademarked fabric programmes and licensed membranes/fills only)
craft_evidence.madein: 0% (no country of origin string on any of the 246 men's PDPs read)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: founded 1960 by Åke Nordin (born Örnsköldsvik 1936) in his basement; Greenland Jacket and G-1000 1968; Kånken 1978
craft_evidence.process: partial: G-1000 plus Greenland Wax re-proofing documented as a care process; no making process described
craft_evidence.reasoning: Fjällräven names no factories, makers or mills on its product pages and states no country of origin on any of the 246 men's styles read; its production page speaks only of a Code of Conduct, audits and FLA membership. What it does document is a dated, placed founding (1960, Åke Nordin, Örnsköldsvik) and its own fabric system (G-1000 with Greenland Wax), which is tech rather than craft. That is a 2 at most: heritage with receipts but nothing checkable about who makes the clothes or where.

ownership.owner: Fenix Outdoor International AG (Nasdaq Stockholm, FOI B); Nordin family and related companies hold 61.5% of capital value and 85.2% of votes; Martin Nordin Executive Chairman and CEO (annual report 2024)

opview: “Enabling and inspiring more people to experience nature was Åke's vision and we now make it our mission.” — Fjällräven (house voice), Fjällräven, Our History page
